item.title: Syrian Kurds return home to celebrate Nowruz for the first time since exile
item.summary: Nowruz, the Farsi-language word for “new year,” is an ancient Persian festival that is also celebrate by Kurds in Syria, Turkey and Iraq as well as Iran. It is characterized by colorful street festivals and torch-bearing processions winding their way into the mountains.

item.title: War in the Middle East: Lebanon's mental health crisis deepens
item.summary: Lebanon has been mired in conflicts and crises for decades, the worst of which was the 15 year civil war that erupted in 1975 and which divided the country into warring sectarian fiefdoms.

item.title: US to send more Marines to Middle East as Trump hints at wind-down
item.summary: Three weeks into an escalating war in the Middle East, Iran threatened to expand its retaliatory attacks to include recreational and tourist sites worldwide, as the U.S. announced it was sending more warships and Marines to the region.

item.title: War in the Middle East: Syria's governement vows to avoid regional escalation
item.summary: Syrian President Ahmed al- Sharaa said Friday he is working to keep his country away from conflict, against the backdrop of the Middle East war, stressing that his government is on good terms with all regional countries.

item.title: €5 billion aimed at offsetting the economic impact of the Middle East conflict
item.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez announced a five billion euro ($5.8 billion) package aimed at offsetting the economic impact of the Middle East conflict, including a "drastic reduction" in energy taxes.
